ui_bugs.issue: Header is NOT actually sticky — scrolls off with content despite `sticky top-0`. Root cause: `html, body, #root { overflow-x: hidden }` (index.css line 107) creates an overflow context on #root that breaks the sticky positioning of the header (its containing block becomes #root which doesn't itself scroll, so header moves with content). Requirement 'header must STAY fixed' fails visually.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Header sticky bug: reproduce on /salary page — scroll window down; header data-testid=top-header should remain at viewport top (getBoundingClientRect().top === 0) but currently moves off-screen (top negative). Cause: #root overflow-x:hidden. Everything else in this batch is green.
rca of the issue: position:sticky computes its containing block from the nearest ancestor with a scroll mechanism. When #root has `overflow-x: hidden`, browsers designate #root as a scroll container for the sticky element, but #root itself is not scrolled (document/body is). Result: header inside #root simply translates with the document flow instead of pinning to the viewport top. Fix by removing `overflow-x: hidden` from the #root rule (keep on html, body) or moving the sticky header outside of #root — recommended: change index.css line 107 to `html, body { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: hidden; overscroll-behavior-x: none; }` and drop #root from that selector, or set `#root { overflow-x: clip; }` in modern browsers which does not create a scroll container.
